Methylxanthine pharmacology

A researcher studies theophylline’s bronchodilator actions in airway smooth muscle. One mechanism involves reducing cyclic nucleotide breakdown rather than stimulating an adrenergic receptor directly. Which enzyme activity is inhibited in this proposed mechanism?

  1. Acetylcholinesterase
  2. Cyclooxygenase-1 exclusively
  3. 5-lipoxygenase
  4. Angiotensin-converting enzyme
  5. Phosphodiesterase
Answer and explanation

Phosphodiesterase

Phosphodiesterase inhibition can increase intracellular cyclic nucleotides; theophylline also has other actions.

Option explanations

Phosphodiesterase: Phosphodiesterase inhibition can increase intracellular cyclic nucleotides; theophylline also has other actions.

Acetylcholinesterase: Its inhibition would increase cholinergic signaling.

Cyclooxygenase-1 exclusively: That is not the cyclic nucleotide breakdown enzyme.

5-lipoxygenase: This is the target of zileuton.

Angiotensin-converting enzyme: ACE does not directly degrade cyclic nucleotides.
